title: Last band: Young Tuxedo, Black Diamond Band and Jack Carey
summary: Eddie says he last played with the Young Tuxedo band. He lists the Black Diamond Band's members, how the Island Queen job broke it up, and a cousin's reuse of the Golden Rule name. Jack Carey then took him to Montgomery.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were you playing with right before you quit?
Who was I playing with? Yeah. When I quit? Uh-huh. I was playing with, no, it wasn't Chris Kelly. Did you tell you about this? No. I was playing with a young tuxedo band.

Now, the band that Paul made of, I guess they ain't got that in the record, called the Black Diamond Band. They had Josiah on drum. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Yank on Cranbourne. Sonny Allen, Ray Allen, we called him. He was on corner. Albert Snyder, second corner. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Mm-hm. The Island Queen had come in, Sidney J. Bean broke that band, and he took Paul away from us. Like they grabbed him right for us. And so, real quick, we started scatting. So, Mireille Vaughan come along, he made up a band. That's my cousin. Well, he took the old name that we had, Golden Rule. He kept the band about a year and something. He took the band. That made up, played at Boston's Park. So, Jack Carey come got me to go to Montgomery, play with him.
Jack Carey. You know what I mean?
He was saying, Jack Carey, they ain't told you nothing about him.
That people ain't told you nothing about Jack Carey.
Jack Carey? Jack Carey. Jack Carey.
See if he's in here. He's a tramo friend.
Uh, so you went to Montgomery? Yeah. Huh?
Nice to meet you. So, you went to Montgomery with Jack Carey? Yeah, Montgomery with Jack Carey.
